meta.title: Conflict Watchlist
meta.notes: Analyst-maintained register. Each review: (1) set reviewDate/previousReviewDate, (2) for every item move `prev` <- `now` on the five dimensions and then set the new `now`, (3) rewrite `changes`, `next` and `csi` for what is true THIS week only, (4) record any state move in `history`. The dashboard derives attention rank, movements, changed-dimension flags, staleness and the brief signal — do not type those in. This is a watchlist, not a news archive: keep `changes` to what materially moved since the previous review, and `next` to named, checkable indicators.

1.name: Priority Conflicts
1.desc: High relevance to the Army — followed every week in the brief.

2.name: Active Regional & Escalation Watches
2.desc: Regional theatres where escalation would change Singapore's or the Army's picture.

3.name: Baseline Regional Research Reserve
3.desc: Held for pattern and case-study value; reviewed on trigger or on the monthly cycle.

Priority.desc: Direct strategic relevance or high Army learning value.

Active.desc: Material trend, escalation, or regional relevance.

Watch.desc: Baseline monitoring; no current learning priority.

Archive.desc: Reserve — retained for reference and pattern work; revisit only on a named trigger.

CSI Flash.desc: Same-day short note: a threshold was crossed or Singapore exposure changed.

Weekly awareness post.desc: One item in this week's brief or awareness post.

Monthly pattern review.desc: Feed the monthly tactical-learning / pattern cycle.

Quarterly candidate.desc: Candidate for a quarterly deep-dive or case study.

attentionScore.desc: Deterministic, explainable rank. state (Priority 40 / Active 25 / Watch 10 / Archive 0) + escalation risk (Severe 20 / High 15 / Moderate 8 / Low 2) + 5 per dimension that changed since the previous review + 10 if the state moved up + CSI action (Flash 20 / Weekly 10 / Monthly 5 / Quarterly 3 / Dashboard 0) + Singapore exposure (High 8 / Moderate 4 / Low 0) + tier (T1 6 / T2 3 / T3 0). Items flagged ignore-for-now are shown but ranked last.

items.name: Russia–Ukraine
items.whyNow: Ukraine's declared 40-day pressure campaign and the confirmation of FPV-as-interceptor make this the richest adaptation feed of the week.
changes: Zelenskyy authorised a 40-day campaign against Russian energy, Crimea supply routes and logistics hubs; Donetsk front static and ISW no longer forecasts a Russian seizure of Donetsk.
FPV drones confirmed as repeatable Shahed interceptors over Crimea; production-chain strike on the Titan-Barrikady missile plant with an FP-5 Flamingo.
Crimea under state of emergency (fuel sales halted, rolling power cuts); Russia concentrating air defence on Moscow and the Kerch Bridge.

next.text: Pre-summit diplomatic engagements in Moscow ahead of US-led tracking initiatives.
next.ifSeen: Confirms a live talks track; watch for a strike pause as a bargaining signal.

next.text: Large Russian retaliatory strike package on Kyiv energy or C2 in answer to the Moscow drone campaign.
next.ifSeen: Weekly awareness post on saturation volume and interceptor stocks.

next.text: End of the declared 40-day campaign window — did Russian posture or logistics visibly change?
next.ifSeen: Monthly pattern review: deep-strike campaign as coercive lever.

next.text: Russian infiltration of Kostiantynivka turns into encirclement or a confirmed withdrawal.
next.ifSeen: Phase check: attritional war vs operational breakthrough.

csi.rationale: FPV-as-interceptor and production-chain targeting are directly transferable C-UAS and fires-planning lessons; volume-saturation fires remains the quarterly pattern candidate.

items.name: Israel–Palestine (Gaza)
items.whyNow: Escalation risk moved up: Hamas has not accepted the disarmament clauses and the risk of Israel resuming large-scale operations is rising, while organised civilian opposition to Hamas surfaced publicly.
changes: 'June 26 Revolution' protests planned at 18 sites were suppressed; Hamas used four hospitals as control and interrogation nodes.
IDF holds ~64% of Gaza with a stated aim of 70%; no Phase 2 timeline exists and Clauses 8–9 (weapons restrictions, stabilisation force) remain unaccepted.
Escalation risk raised from Moderate to High on the brief's assessment that a return to large-scale operations is increasingly likely.

next.text: UN Security Council open briefing and closed consultations on International Stabilisation Force deployment bottlenecks.
next.ifSeen: Note ISF force-generation and mandate gaps for the stabilisation case study.

next.text: Hamas formally accepts or rejects Clauses 8 and 9 — the last gate before Israel restarts large-scale operations.
next.ifSeen: Rejection → move to Priority and CSI Flash on phase change.

next.text: IDF 'Yellow Line' berms extend beyond the 64% line toward the stated 70%.
next.ifSeen: Low-signature territorial consolidation pattern for the monthly review.

csi.rationale: Governance-transfer-without-disarmament and civilian-opposition dynamics are stabilisation and CIMIC learning, not a weekly item unless the ceasefire breaks.

items.name: US–Israel–Iran

phase.now: Post-war MOU under a fragile stand-down

items.whyNow: Hormuz transit is conditional and reversible, the 60-day final-deal clock is running, and the week produced both maritime strikes and a stand-down — the highest Singapore-exposure item on the list.
changes: Tit-for-tat Gulf strikes (Iranian drone strikes on merchant ships; US strikes on Iranian surveillance, air-defence and drone sites) before a fresh 28–29 June stand-down.

Phase moved from ceasefire-under-strain to a post-war MOU: US lifted Iran oil sanctions for 60 days; nuclear working groups start; southern Omani lane open day and night, central channel still restricted with ~80 mines uncleared.
Cyber domain expansion: ~4,800 Iranian hostile cyber incidents against Israeli networks in one month, three times last year's volume.

next.text: US–Iran emergency talks in Doha on the Strait of Hormuz impasse.
next.ifSeen: Outcome sets whether transit normalises or the 48-hour permit regime hardens; CSI Flash on any change to transit terms.

next.text: 60-day final-deal deadline under the MOU.
next.ifSeen: Missed deadline → escalation indicator; expect blockade or re-closure signalling in the preceding fortnight.

next.text: Central-channel mine clearance completes (≈80 mines) and daily transits return toward the ~70-ship pre-war baseline.
next.ifSeen: Downgrade SG exposure to Moderate; move CSI action to weekly.

next.text: Any strike on merchant shipping or US basing after the 29 June stand-down.
next.ifSeen: CSI Flash the same day.

csi.rationale: Hormuz terms bear directly on Singapore fuel and shipping exposure; Shahed-as-anti-helicopter and cyber volume-saturation feed the monthly pattern review.

history.note: Baseline: Hormuz crisis, direct Singapore exposure.

items.name: Israel–Lebanon
items.whyNow: Moved up to Priority: the 26 June Washington Framework creates a Military Coordination Group that regional partners may be asked to join, while the IDF struck Lebanon hours after signing and Hezbollah refused the deal.
changes: 14-point trilateral framework signed in Washington on 26 June: two LAF pilot zones tied to phased Hezbollah disarmament, no timeline for full Israeli withdrawal, no enforcement mechanism.
IDF drone strike in southern Lebanon within hours of signing; security zone maintained; Hezbollah publicly rejected the framework.
Singapore exposure raised to Moderate because the framework's Military Coordination Group may seek regional-partner contributions.

next.text: First LAF–mediator working-group sessions on pilot-zone boundaries south of the Litani.
next.ifSeen: A dated first handover is the framework's first real test.

next.text: Composition and terms of reference of the Military Coordination Group for Lebanon announced.
next.ifSeen: Scope what a contribution would require (ROE alongside IDF and LAF); brief up.

next.text: Hezbollah retaliation for post-signing strikes, or an IDF strike inside a designated pilot zone.
next.ifSeen: Framework at risk → Weekly awareness post.

csi.rationale: The MCG question is time-sensitive for planners; the prepared ATGM-plus-drone ambush against armour is the quarterly anti-armour candidate.

history.note: Washington Framework signed; Military Coordination Group may seek regional partners; fighting continues.

items.name: Thailand–Cambodia
items.whyNow: Quiet on the ground; the watch is procedural (conciliation chair deadline) and about below-threshold signalling and Chinese capability deliveries.
changes: RTAF issued a formal clarification on F-16 night flights along the border; Cambodia characterised them as military signalling — a calibrated, deniable messaging pattern with miscalculation risk.
Four UNCLOS conciliators appointed; the five-member commission must elect a chairperson by about 16 July; land border remains economically severed by Cambodian decree.
No kinetic incidents; Thai National Anti-Drone Centre approved and stood up.

next.text: Conciliation commission elects a chairperson.
next.ifSeen: Missed deadline → legal track stalls; watch for Cambodian escalation at sea or on trade.

next.text: Thai economic countermeasure to Cambodia's land-trade blockade.
next.ifSeen: Trade coercion cycle → move CSI action to weekly.

next.text: Second Chinese tank batch (of the 93 ordered) lands at Sihanoukville or tanks leave containers.
next.ifSeen: Grey-zone capability-building under a ceasefire; monthly review.

csi.rationale: Nothing to publish this week; the permanent C-UAS centre and the signalling pattern are already in the monthly cycle via the Capabilities tab.

next.text: Announced timeline for national elections and sanctions decisions on the oil sector.
next.ifSeen: Transition consolidating → consider moving to Watch.

next.text: Armed-group (colectivo / ELN) violence against the transition authorities or US personnel.

items.name: South China Sea
items.whyNow: Steady-state coercion around Philippine-held features; high Singapore exposure through sea lines of communication and ASEAN centrality, with the Code of Conduct on the Philippine chairmanship's agenda.
changes: No material change since the previous review; China Coast Guard and maritime-militia presence around Scarborough and Second Thomas Shoal continues at the established pattern.

next.text: A Philippine resupply or patrol is blocked with injuries, a vessel is boarded, or a collision causes casualties.
next.ifSeen: CSI Flash; move to Priority.

next.text: Code of Conduct milestones under the Philippine ASEAN chairmanship ahead of the year-end summits.
next.ifSeen: Framework text agreed → Weekly awareness post.

next.text: PLA Navy or CCG surge around Sabina Shoal or Scarborough enforcement of the declared 'nature reserve'.
next.ifSeen: Tempo up → re-check state.

csi.rationale: Repetitive pattern; publish only on an incident threshold. Grey-zone coercion sequencing stays in the monthly pattern set.

items.name: Taiwan Strait
items.whyNow: Adaptation behaviour moved up: Taiwan's civilian drone-literacy programme (Kuma Academy) is a scalable whole-of-society mobilisation model with direct Army learning value.
changes: Taiwan's Kuma Academy launched a fully booked civilian drone training programme (~75 citizens a month, GPS-free manual flying to bypass jamming) — civil resilience explicitly modelled on Ukraine.
PLA air and maritime activity around the island continues at the established pattern; no large named exercise this week.

next.text: Han Kuang annual exercise (live-fire and whole-of-society phases).
next.ifSeen: Watch civil-defence integration and reserve mobilisation drills for the monthly review.

next.text: PLA large-scale joint drill announced around a political trigger (transit, arms sale, legislative vote).
next.ifSeen: Escalation risk to High; Weekly awareness post.

next.text: Sustained PLA presence inside the 24 nm contiguous zone or a blockade-style inspection regime.
next.ifSeen: Move to Priority; CSI Flash.

csi.rationale: Civilian drone literacy and whole-of-society mobilisation are Army learning; no publication trigger this week.

phase.prev: Proxy pressure linked to the Iran track
